name: LCROSS
short_status: Impacted Cabeus crater Oct 9, 2009; water ice confirmed Nov 13, 2009, quantified at 155 kg in the plume (Science, Oct 2010).
tagline: NASA · United States · Impactor · 2009 · The robotic return Success
stats: water vapor and ice measured in the ejecta plume (± 12 kg)
water ice by mass in Cabeus regolith (± 2.9%)
impact speed of the 2,305 kg Centaur stage
total mission cost, riding shotgun on LRO's rocket

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 18 June 2009, 21:32 UT, Atlas V 401 from Cape Canaveral (shared with LRO)

facts.label: Impactor
facts.value: Spent Centaur upper stage, nominal 5,081 lb (2,305 kg) at impact

facts.label: Shepherding Spacecraft impact
facts.value: 9 October 2009, 11:36 UT, after flying through the plume

facts.label: Water detected
facts.value: 155 ± 12 kg of water vapor and ice in the instrument field of view

facts.label: Regolith ice concentration
facts.value: 5.6 ± 2.9% water ice by mass at the impact site

facts.label: Mission cost
facts.value: $79 million (cost-capped secondary payload, launch shared with LRO)

facts.label: Science payload
facts.value: Nine instruments on the 621 kg (dry) Shepherding Spacecraft: 5 cameras, 3 spectrometers, 1 photometer

facts.label: Management / builder
facts.value: NASA Ames Research Center (mission), Northrop Grumman, Redondo Beach (spacecraft)

facts.label: Crater (measured 2024)
facts.value: About 22 m diameter at 84.6780 S, 48.6926 W, located with ShadowCam and Mini-RF (Fassett et al. 2024, GRL, gold open access), roughly 80 m from the earlier Marshall et al. weighted-average estimate and well within its error bars

facts.label: Results announced
facts.value: 13 November 2009: NASA confirms water in the plume spectra

timeline: NASA selects LCROSS as LRO's low-cost, fast-track companion mission
Launch at 21:32 UT on Atlas V 401 from Cape Canaveral, with LRO
Inertial reference unit fault triggers thruster firings that burn ~140 kg of propellant, more than half the remaining fuel
Impact target switched from Cabeus A to Cabeus proper on hydrogen data from LRO, Lunar Prospector, Chandrayaan-1 and Kaguya
Centaur impacts Cabeus at 11:31 UT at 2.5 km/s; Shepherding Spacecraft flies through the plume and impacts at 11:36 UT
NASA announces the mission found water in the permanently shadowed crater
Science publishes the quantified result: 155 ± 12 kg of water in the field of view, 5.6 ± 2.9% ice by mass
ShadowCam and Mini-RF finally locate the 22 m Centaur crater inside the Cabeus permanently shadowed region
